turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Hey [PERSON_1], hey [PERSON_2]. How's the week going? [PERSON_2], I saw the storm track, are you guys buried?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Buried is generous. We're at like 140 percent of normal claims volume since Sunday. I've got people doing twelve-hour shifts and the after-hours queue is the worst part.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Ouch. And you're still in hurricane season through November, right?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Yeah, technically through the end of November. October is usually the worst of it for us.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Sorry, I'm coming in hot, I just got back from that marketing analytics conference in Chicago last night. My brain is still half in a hotel ballroom.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Oh nice, how was it?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Good, actually. Lots of sessions on attribution, like, which is funny because half the room is still fighting the same last-click argument we were having in 2019.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: But it was good to get out of the building.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Any um, sessions that were actually useful?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: One on um, offline conversion imports, which, you know, relevant. I took a bunch of notes. I'll send them your way if there's anything worth stealing.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Please do. Okay, so, agenda. I want to walk through Q3 numbers, then a couple of items you flagged, and [PERSON_4] said she'd join for the last ten minutes or so.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Sound okay?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Works for me.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Yep.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Cool. So top of the funnel first. [PERSON_1], call volume across tracking numbers was up 11 percent quarter over quarter, which tracks with the auto campaign you launched in August.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Google Ads offline conversions are flowing, match rate held steady. Anything surprising on your side?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Not really, the volume's where we we expected. The one thing, um, and I've been meaning to bring this up, is the spam filtering.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Not a huge deal but it's noisy.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay, tell me more.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: So the spam filter is catching a chunk of our after-hours roadside calls, people calling from the shoulder of the highway, and they're dropping out of my reports.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: And I only found it because one of the claims folks mentioned a call that never showed up in the dashboard.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay. Do you have a rough sense of how many, or is it more anecdotal right now?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Anecdotal so far. I'd guess a couple dozen a month, but I don't want to quote that. Um, the pattern seems to be short calls from mobile numbers, and the audio quality is rough because, you know, highway.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: That makes sense. Let me take that back and have the team look at how those calls are being classified, and we can look at whether there's a way to keep them out of the the spam bucket.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: I don't want to guess at a fix on the call.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: That's all I'm asking. It's not breaking anything, it's just, my roadside numbers look soft and they're not.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Got it. I'll follow up by end of next week with what we find.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Perfect.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: [PERSON_2], let's talk contact center. Genesys routing's been stable, PreSense is firing on the inbound sales queue. How's the agent experience?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Stable, yeah. Screen pops are landing before the agent picks up, which was the whole point. No complaints there.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Good. And QM, you're still scoring the sales queues?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Sales, yes. Claims, no, and that's the thing I wanted to talk about.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: So we've got QM scoring 100 percent of the sales calls against the sales scorecard, and it's been fine. But claims is a different animal.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: A claims call is somebody you know, having the worst week of their life, and the behaviors we're coaching on sales calls don't map.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Right.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: And I've been trying to explain this to my ops leads and I keep not getting it across. It's like, the scorecard has a section on needs discovery and a section on closing, and on a claims call there's no close.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: There's no upsell. So So the agents get dinged for stuff that doesn't apply and then they stop trusting the scores.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: So the scorecard itself is the mismatch, not the scoring engine.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: I think so, but I don't know how to say what I actually want. It's not just swapping words on the scorecard.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: The weighting is different, the call types are different. A fender bender and a total loss are not the same conversation, and I want the scoring to know that.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay, so walk me through an example. Take a total loss call.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Total loss, the agent's job is to absorb the emotion, be clear about next steps, not over-promise on the settlement, and get the person off the phone with a plan.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Empathy is the whole job. Versus a policy question, which is accuracy and speed. Those are opposite scorecards.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: And today you're scoring both against the sales scorecard.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Yeah, which is why for claims we need to grade empathy differently, like a total loss call is not a policy question, and right now I can't build that.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay. Let me make sure I've got it. You want claims scorecards that are segmented by call type, so a total loss call gets graded on a different set of behaviors than a routine policy question, and the weighting reflects that.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Yes. That's it. That's what I've been trying to say for three weeks.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay, I'm going to write that up and take it to the product team. I can't tell you today what's possible, but I want to get your exact example in front of them because the total loss versus policy question distinction is the clearest version of this I've heard.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Good. And I'm happy to get on a call with them if that helps.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: It might. Let me find out first.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Go ahead.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay, last thing before [PERSON_4] joins, Adobe Analytics. Anything you need from me on the integration side?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: No, it's fine. Data's flowing.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Great. Let me grab [PERSON_4].

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Hi everyone, sorry, I'm two minutes late, I was on a call with our Ohio governor's office thing. What did I miss?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: [PERSON_3]'s taking a couple of things back to product, mostly QM for claims.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Good. That's the one I care about most, honestly. Our claims CSAT is fine but the coaching side has been a a gap for a while.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: We're on it. [PERSON_2] gave me a really clear example, so I have something concrete to bring to the team.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Great. And I'll say, since I'm here, the PreSense routing is honestly the best thing we bought last year. My distribution VPs bring it up unprompted, which never happens with technology.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: That's good to hear. The screen pops are landing clean?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Clean. Agents know who they're talking to before they say hello. It's changed the tone of the calls.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Love that. Okay, so where we landed. [PERSON_1], spam classification on after-hours roadside calls, I'll come back to you by end of next week.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: [PERSON_2], claims scorecards, I'll write it up and take it to product. Everything else is steady. Anything I'm missing?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: No, that covers it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Same.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Nothing from me. [PERSON_3], thank you for running these, they're actually useful, which is not something I say uh, about QBRs.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: I'll take it. I'll send notes tomorrow. [PERSON_2], hang in there with the season.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Yeah, thanks. Talk soon.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Bye everyone.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Take care.
